results.title: Major Fitness is rated "Excellent" with 4.3 / 5 on Trustpilot
results.content:
## Great Product. Horrible Customer Service
While the product itself is well made, getting product support from the company is quite frustrating.   
  
One of the flex arms are loose on our new equipment, likely due to a manufacturing error, as the other side is just fine. We have been trying to get support, but they only reply to emails once every 24 hours. Not to mention the replies are usually in the middle of the night, and with less than helpful feedback. Videos and photos have been sent to show the problem, yet no real resolution has been offered.   
  
Today I called because I was frustrated with the email process, and instead of any help, I was told they would email again within 24 hours. [...] Looking at 791 reviews, reviewers overwhelmingly had a great experience with this company. Customers frequently praise the sturdy build, high quality, and smooth operation of the home gym equipment, making daily workouts a breeze. Many people also appreciate the prompt delivery service, clear assembly instructions, and helpful manuals provided with their orders. Some reviewers were not happy with the customer service responsiveness, noting occasional challenges and delays with incorrect replacement parts. Consumers explained that getting support for missing components or wrong cables took longer than expected and required multiple attempts to resolve. Despite these drawbacks, most individuals still consider the fitness machines to be an excellent investment for their homes.See more [...] Image 34: Rated 5 out of 5 stars

Verified

## I did have some issues with the…
I did have some issues with the assembly, the manual could have been much clearer (the video is much more helpful but can be better as well) and a couple of parts were missing. However support was great and all issues were eventually solved. The other thing that could be better was if the labels on the weight stack came from the factory, putting them on one by one wasn’t easy with a few tearing up.  
The quality of the product is amazing. The machine (B17) is very complete, it really does almost substitute for an entire professional gym. It’s very sturdy, looks really high quality, high end, for the price I was expecting something cheaper-looking, in other words the product is well worth the price.

Your communication should be streamlined. Member management software helps to keep track of conversations, instructions, and payments. You should have steps in place to deliver effective communication. If something slips through and there is an error, rectify the problem. Use every mistake as a lesson so that you can update your communication strategy and make sure it doesn’t happen again.

### 5. Broken or Faulty Equipment

Broken or faulty equipment, as well as equipment that’s been left out, can frustrate members. Your customers pay for a service. When you don’t meet that expectation, they start to question why they are paying for a gym membership in the first place. It becomes a problem when members are repeatedly dealing with the same issue. [...] It’s no secret that equipment can break from time to time. But you can do something to keep the complaints surrounding equipment to a minimum. Don’t delay fixing any equipment. This could result in both injuries and frustrated members. Make sure your staff put away all equipment and encourage members to put equipment back after use during your onboarding program.

### 6. Overcrowded Gym

In the normal non-pandemic days of the past, it was frustrating for members to find that they have to wait for equipment or there are too many people around to workout properly. Now, overcrowding poses another risk as it’s more difficult to socially distant when the gym is too crowded. [...] By spreading out your peak hours and notifying members of all your capacity guidelines, they have the right information to avoid crowding. Your gym or health spa may be open at a reduced capacity or hoping to reopen in the near future. Either way, try to entice members in at non-peak times as well as encourage them to use your digital fitness platform from home.

### 7. Last-Minute Cancellations

Last-minute cancellations for classes and one on one personal training sessions are frustrating. That’s not to say that on occasion, you don’t have a valid reason for canceling bookings. But the way you handle cancellations will help you set the right tone.

results.title: Gym Member Complaints: Improve Customer Service - GymMaster
results.content:
Cleanliness and hygiene: From dusty equipment and overflowing bins to lingering smells in the changing rooms, a lack of cleanliness is often the first thing members notice and the most common reason for immediate complaints.
 Broken or faulty equipment: Members pay for access to tools that work, so equipment downtime can grate on them. Seeing an “out of order” sign on your favorite treadmill for days on end can be a major source of frustration.
 Overcrowding: Too many bodies can make it hard for members to stick to their routines, leading to complaints about wait times or a lack of available slots in group classes. [...] Example: Hi Sarah, thank you for sharing your feedback regarding the broken equipment in the functional training zone. We understand how frustrating it is when your workout is interrupted, and we appreciate the patience while we get this sorted. Our team has ordered the replacement parts and we expect the machines to be fully operational by Wednesday. We would like to hear more about your experience to ensure we can improve – would you be open to having a quick chat?

#### Responding to unfair criticisms

When a complaint is exaggerated - or worse, provably untrue - the temptation is to get defensive, to throw blame back at the reviewer, to start an argument. None of these reactions will be good for business. You instead need to: [...] #### Sample scripts

 Social media: “Hi [Name], thanks for the feedback. We want to look into this immediately – please DM us your email or call [phone number] so we can get this sorted for you.”
 Face-to-face: “I can see why that is frustrating, and I’m going to take ownership of this for you. Let me investigate what happened and follow up with you by [time/date] with an update.”
 Email: “Dear [Name], I am sorry for the frustration caused by the recent equipment downtime. We have scheduled the repair for [date] and added a complimentary guest pass to your account as a thank you for your patience.”

results.content:
If equipment quality is one of the issues affecting your member experience, RDX Wholesale offers durable fitness and combat sports gear built for gyms, clubs, and training facilities that need reliable equipment for daily use.

## FAQs

### What are the most common gym complaints from members?

Common gym complaints include broken gym equipment, overcrowding, poor cleanliness, unclear billing, loud music, and unhelpful staff. These common gym problems directly affect member satisfaction and retention.

### How does broken gym equipment affect a gym business?

Broken gym equipment frustrates members, raises safety concerns, and signals poor maintenance. Ongoing problems with gym equipment are one of the fastest ways to lose trust and increase cancellations. [...] ## How Gym Owners Should Respond to Complaints?

Reducing gym complaints starts with a consistent response system. Most members do not expect the gym to be perfect, but they do expect problems to be noticed, acknowledged, and fixed.

Start with complaints that undermine safety, trust, and daily workout quality. Broken equipment, poor cleanliness, billing confusion, overcrowding, and staff behavior should be handled first because they can quickly lead to frustration, bad reviews, and cancellations.

Use member feedback, staff observations, equipment usage data, and cancellation reasons to find repeated patterns. If the same complaint keeps appearing, treat it as an operational problem that needs a permanent fix, not a one-time issue. [...] ### Equipment and Training Floor Complaints

Equipment-related complaints are among the biggest warning signs in your gym. Your members pay for access, convenience, safety, and workout quality. When equipment is unavailable, broken, outdated, or poorly maintained, they quickly question the value of their membership.

Here are the primary equipment-related complaints gym members face:

1. #### Equipment Frequently Unavailable

Your gym members get frustrated when machines are always occupied, especially during peak hours. This makes workouts feel rushed and unproductive. The access to equipment becomes a daily struggle, and motivation drops.
